chief_complaint: Post‑myocardial infarction follow‑up with focus on cardiovascular risk management
history_of_present_illness: The patient suffered an acute NSTEMI on 2019‑04‑24 followed by a documented history of MI. He was placed on dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin and prasugrel) and high‑intensity statin, beta‑blocker, ACE‑inhibitor and thiazide, suggesting percutaneous coronary intervention. In early 2020 he experienced severe COVID‑19 infection complicated by pneumonia, hypoxemia, and an acute deep venous thrombosis treated with enoxaparin. Since then his chronic conditions—including hypertension, metabolic syndrome, obesity, pre‑diabetes, anemia, and chronic musculoskeletal pain—have persisted. He remains employed full‑time at age 75, reports ongoing stress, and is on a moderate polypharmacy regimen.

active_problems.name: Acute non‑ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include acute deep venous thrombosis (2020‑04‑23), COVID‑19 infection with associated pneumonia, hypoxemia, fever, cough, loss of taste, fatigue, joint pain, and a suspected COVID‑19 episode (2020‑04‑10). The patient also has a remote surgical history of appendectomy (1966). These resolved events were managed and have since resolved.
